recipe_audit.finding: The three stored rungs are TWO mesh recipes, and no knob moves twice. coarse -> medium refines the background blockMesh and holds the near-body levels fixed; medium -> production refines the near-body levels (refinementSurfaces body level, the eMesh feature level and the nearBody region level, all three at once) and holds the background blockMesh IDENTICAL. Read from each rung's own system/snappyHexMeshDict and system/blockMeshDict, with each cell count read from that rung's own constant/polyMesh/owner header and matched against the count stored in levels[]. A pure background change IS a uniform refinement -- snappyHexMesh subdivides background cells by 2^level, so scaling the background scales h everywhere with one ratio r -- which is the step b52.json's recipe_audit accepts. A pure level change is NOT: it subdivides only at the surface, along the feature edges and inside the nearBody box, leaving the farfield h untouched, so there is no single r for that step and a Richardson expansion in one h has nothing to expand in. Each of these ladders therefore contains ONE valid refinement pair (coarse -> medium) and one step that is not a grid refinement, and the invalid step is the TOP one: the finest rung, the mesh the act solves and the credentials wall counts cells for, is the rung not connected to the rest of its ladder by a valid step. Two rungs cannot yield an observed order, so the observed_order and richardson_extrapolated in the numerical block below are fitted across a step that is not a refinement.
recipe_audit.cause: sdk/workflows/geometry_study.py, refinement_rungs(). Every act on this path runs refinement=3, so base=3, medium_level=max(2,2)=2 and coarse_level=max(2,1)=2 -- the floor collapses the coarse level onto the medium level. That makes coarse_level == medium_level true, which is the condition that gives the coarse rung, and only the coarse rung, block_scale 0.7. The function's docstring says 'Each rung steps the whole level family down one'; at refinement 3 that is false, and the docstring itself records why the second knob exists: 'when the floor would make two rungs identical, the coarser one also scales the background-mesh divisions so the cell budgets stay distinct; the runtime cell-count guard still refuses to report a study if they do not.' The guard added checks DISTINCTNESS. Distinctness is not comparability, and nothing downstream was ever asked whether the rungs were comparable.

knob_moved.coarse_to_medium: background blockMesh only (a uniform h refinement)
knob_moved.medium_to_production: near-body levels only, background identical (NOT a uniform h refinement)

step_evidence.reading: The two steps move Cd by amounts that do not scale with their nominal cell ratios, and the direction of the mismatch follows the geometry: on the two thin wings the near-body step dominates, on the two blunt Ahmed bodies the farfield step does. That consistency is evidence the two steps measure different things rather than the same thing twice.

mesh_generation_scatter.method: One replicate mesh at each rung's nominal resolution, reached by a different background division triple; every other file byte-identical to its twin, verified by diff -r on system/ and 0.orig/ and md5 on the STL. Solved identically at 4 MPI ranks with residualControl 1e-4.
mesh_generation_scatter.finding: Scatter falls monotonically with cell count and follows an inverse-square law: scatter x N^2 is 0.051, 0.056, 0.052, 0.050 (units 1e9) across a 3.74x range in N, constant to plus or minus 6 percent, fitted exponent 2.024. So mesh-construction scatter on this body is a COARSE-mesh problem that refinement cures, not a fine-mesh problem refinement causes. The r4 failure is therefore not the scatter growing -- the r4 scatter is the smallest measured, 1.799e-04 -- it is the INCREMENT collapsing by a factor of 44 in one step, from 1.927e-03 to 4.412e-05. The p = 24.048 remains an artefact; the mechanism stated in W3_WING_VALID_FAMILY_RESULTS.md section 3 was half wrong and the half that was wrong is the direction. The dangerous rung is the COARSEST: at 140,545 cells the scatter is 2.599e-03, 21.6 percent of the value and 158 percent of the next refinement step.

predictions_scored.P1 scatter grows with cell count, larges: FALSE and exactly backwards on this body: scatter falls monotonically by a factor of 14.45
predictions_scored.P2 r1 and r2 scatters each under 20 perc: FALSE: r1 at 158 percent and r2 at 68 percent
predictions_scored.P2's stated consequence is corrected, no: P2 said that failing it would mean these ladders were never measuring discretization at any rung. That is too strong: the 4412's r2 and r3 and the 0012's r3 are clean at 2, 15 and 21 percent. What is true is narrower and worse-placed -- the scatter rivals or exceeds the increment at the COARSEST rung on both bodies, and every three-rung ladder stored in this corpus puts two of its three rungs at or below that resolution.

Both converged on residualControl at 1e-4 and both are settled to 2-sigma below 6e-07, three to four orders of magnitude below the difference between them.
published_verdict_not_reproducible.finding: The row's VERDICT is not reproducible. The sentence the wall prints -- 'outside the +/-30% band' -- is true of one mesh and false of another built to the same recipe at the same resolution by the same generator, both converged and settled.
published_verdict_not_reproducible.not_grounds_for_an_upgrade: This must not be read as the NACA 0012 agreeing with Abbott and von Doenhoff to 5 percent. A verdict moving toward agreement deserves MORE scrutiny than one moving away. The honest reading damages both verdicts equally: this mesh family cannot resolve the difference between '5 percent off' and '34 percent off', because mesh construction alone moves the answer by 21.6 percent of its own value while the whole question is whether it is 30 percent off. The consequence is that the row should not state a verdict its evidence cannot support -- not that it should state a better one.
published_verdict_not_reproducible.envelope_in_proportion: Separately, this body's published envelope of +/- 0.015 is 5.8 times WIDER than the mesh scatter, so the scatter sits inside it, as it does on the Ahmed 25 degree (19 percent) and the NACA 0015 sail (7 percent). But that envelope is also 125.45 percent of the value it decorates, and an envelope larger than its own quantity will contain almost anything. Passing that check is weak evidence and is recorded as weak. The verdict is the part of the row a reader acts on, and the verdict is what fails.
published_verdict_not_reproducible.belongs_to: the open ruling w3-a-declined-ladder-still-publishes-an-envelope, which already covers this row and now has a sharper second question: may a credential print a pass/fail verdict against a reference when an independently generated mesh at the same resolution moves the measured value across the boundary?
published_verdict_not_reproducible.cheapest_next_experiment: A third and fourth replicate at the same resolution, to say whether 0.01205 or 0.00945 is the outlier or whether the distribution is simply that wide. Two points give a range, not a distribution. About 3 core-minutes per replicate at 4 ranks on tonight's measurement.

four_mesh_sample.verdicts: 1 of 4 OUTSIDE the +/-30% band, and it is the one the wall publishes
four_mesh_sample.not_a_refinement_effect: Cell counts span 127,857 to 140,545, a 10 percent range, and this ladder's own trend is Cd FALLING with refinement -- 0.012052 / 0.010406 / 0.008479 as cells go 140k / 224k / 358k. The published mesh is the FINEST of the four and gives the HIGHEST drag, the opposite of the trend. A coarser mesh giving a lower Cd cannot be explained by resolution.
four_mesh_sample.what_it_sharpens: It is now not merely that the verdict is irreproducible: the mesh the credential was built on is the LEAST representative of the four, and it is the one whose reading produced the failing verdict on the wall.
four_mesh_sample.still_not_an_upgrade: n = 4 is four; the sample standard deviation of 1.1979e-03 is 11.5 percent of the mean; and a mean of four arbitrarily chosen meshes is not a converged answer either -- it is four readings of a quantity this family cannot pin down. This licenses REMOVING a verdict, not replacing it with a better one.
four_mesh_sample.next_experiment_named_not_run: The same four-mesh spread at the 358,430-cell resolution, where the measured scatter is 4.064e-04 rather than 2.599e-03, a sixth the size. If the spread there places the body cleanly inside or outside the band, the credential has a resolution at which it can honestly be stated. About 20 core-minutes at 4 ranks on tonight's measurement.

the_ladder_crosses_the_reference.prior_art: R4 recorded this pattern on the Ahmed 25 degree -- 'the solution passes through the experiment near 144,000 cells rather than converging to it' -- and it had never been checked on this body. Two of two bodies checked now do it.

same_test_at_the_finer_rung.stated_against_my_own_interest: It would be easy to read this as 'the credential passes at the right rung', and that reading is available: 4 of 4 inside at a spread 2.7 times tighter. It is NOT the reading taken, for three reasons. (1) Passing through is not converging to -- the ladder is above the reference at 140k and below it at 358k, so landing inside the band at r3 is where the sweep happened to be. (2) The r3 value is a better-resolved UNVALIDATED value: the r3->r4 increment of -4.4e-05 is below this rung's own mesh scatter, so the ladder is unresolved above r3, and every rung is addLayers false at chord Reynolds 1.0e6. (3) n = 4 at each of two resolutions is not a distribution.
same_test_at_the_finer_rung.what_it_does_establish: The wall's verdict is determined by a resolution choice nobody has defended. Grade 140,580 cells and you get an irreproducible fail; grade 358,430 and you get a reproducible pass. That choice sits in the record implicitly and should be made explicitly and argued -- a question for the open ruling, not a licence to move the row.
same_test_at_the_finer_rung.corrects_an_earlier_number: W3_MESH_NOISE_FLOOR_RESULTS.md reports the scatter falling as N^-2, exponent 2.024, 'constant to plus or minus 6 percent'. That came from a SINGLE pairwise difference at each of four resolutions. With four meshes at each of two resolutions the same body gives an implied exponent of 1.46 from the range and 1.42 from the standard deviation, against 1.98 from the single pair. Those are different statistics and not directly comparable, so 2.024 is not wrong on its own terms -- but the exponent is not pinned down and the tidy inverse square should not be carried forward as established. The direction, falling rather than rising, is unaffected and was the part that mattered.

recipe_fork_ruling_2026_08_25.ruling: An observed order computed across a RECIPE-FORKED gap is NOT A RESULT. It is a slope fitted across a CHANGE OF EXPERIMENT (docs/charters/VERIFICATION_CHARTER.md section 3.2), and under CLAUDE.md rule 5 a row whose triple is not a valid CONVERGING triple is NOT A RESULT whatever its value.
recipe_fork_ruling_2026_08_25.says_nothing_against_the_solves: THIS SAYS NOTHING AGAINST THE UNDERLYING SOLVES. Every rung ran; every coefficient was measured on a real mesh by a real solver; every cell count, force history and convergence log stands exactly as recorded. The ruling is against the GRID-CONVERGENCE CLAIMS BUILT ON THEM and against nothing else.
recipe_fork_ruling_2026_08_25.one_way_door: The affected rows move TOWARD NOT A RESULT, which CLAUDE.md rule 5 permits -- never back. In rule 5 own words the gate "can only turn a PASS or GATE FAIL INTO NOT A RESULT, never the reverse." Nothing here turns any NOT A RESULT back into a PASS.
recipe_fork_ruling_2026_08_25.sweep: 461 candidate directories, 422 parsed, 14 ladders assembled: 7 RECIPE-FORKED, 4 recipe-clean, 3 unauditable
recipe_fork_ruling_2026_08_25.instrument_stated_limit: similarity_failures() treats ANY change of a block grading as a similarity failure ("regraded cells are not scaled cells"). That is CORRECT for the uniform-background snappyHexMesh ladders this sweep covers and WRONG for a correctly-built GRADED ladder, which must change its grading string as it refines precisely in order to keep the first cell scaling. F12 repaired RAE 2822 ladder is exactly such a family, so running recipe_audit.py against it would report a SPURIOUS FORK. A check that overstates its reach is worse than none. See section 5 of the record.
